# Source 110 — CGTN Opinion: Why the Global South will have more leverage than ever in the future of AI

- **URL:** https://news.cgtn.com/news/2026-08-10/Why-Global-South-will-have-more-leverage-than-ever-in-the-future-of-AI-1PurCThjGMw/p.html
- **Author:** Saxon Zvina (special commentator; Harare-based consultant, BRI Think Tank member)
- **Published:** 2026-08-10
- **Type:** Opinion article (CGTN Opinion)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- Xi outlined **four proposals for global AI governance** at the 2026 WAIC: openness/win-win cooperation with innovation-driven development; risk awareness and secure/controllable AI; inclusiveness and mutual learning among civilizations; solidarity and improved global governance.
- **More than 100 UN member states — most from the Global South — have not participated in major international AI governance initiatives.**
- Accelerated AI adoption could contribute **as much as $1.5 trillion to Africa's economy by 2030** (attributed to "studies"; AfDB/UNDP initiatives envision tens of millions of jobs).
- Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt, and South Africa have begun developing national AI strategies.
- Open-source models such as **DeepSeek and Qwen** offer high-performance AI at significantly lower costs, enabling localized applications in education, healthcare, agriculture, finance, public administration, and indigenous languages.
- Chinese companies are partners in Africa's digital infrastructure (data centers, telecom, connectivity); **Zimbabwe's High-Performance Computing Center** cited.
- China announced (per Xi's WAIC address) **5,000 AI training opportunities** for developing countries over five years and **AI application cooperation centers** serving ASEAN, AU, Arab League, BRICS, SCO, and Latin American partners.
- **WAICO, founded by 29 countries**, is described as an independent intergovernmental organization operating per UN Charter principles, aiming at technology sharing, policy dialogue, capacity building, collaborative governance.
- Argues the Global South's leverage comes from markets, young populations, and data resources (agriculture, biodiversity, climate, public health); G77+China call for capacity building/financing/equitable participation; "sovereign AI" concept.

## Verification notes
- Consistent with draft.md usage (Global South leverage, 5,000 training, WAICO 29 founders, open-source models).
- Opinion piece by a named commentator affiliated with a BRI think tank — advocacy framing; factual items (5,000 training, 29-country WAICO, four proposals) match the official WAIC announcements (sources 103/113).
- The $1.5T-by-2030 Africa figure is attributed generically to "studies" — not independently sourced in the article.
